span.term: incoming activity that exceeds a dynamical threshold ignites a self-supporting reverberating cell assembly which sustains the conscious content and broadcasts it to distant sites

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: global broadcasting frees information from encapsulated circuits and makes it available to many processors, including the ones that formulate verbal reports, which is why conscious information is reportable

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: during ignition the workspace is mobilised as a whole, with the non-selected neurons actively inhibited, which blocks a second simultaneous ignition and produces the serial bottleneck
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: spontaneous prestimulus fluctuations barely affect the fast feedforward stage but strongly bias the slow NMDA-based reverberating stage, so an identical stimulus ignites on some trials and not others, producing all-or-none perception

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a weak stimulus produces a feedforward wave that cannot recruit enough self-sustaining reverberation, so it dies out before the late global activation and stays subliminal

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: because far more workspace neurons are laterally inhibited than activated, the summed scalp signal during ignition is net positive, which is why conscious access shows up as the positive P3b
span.note: status: the paper's own words: can explain why

span.label: The supporting simulations implement only a small fragment of the proposed architecture

span.label: Lesion and TMS evidence does not establish that prefrontal contribution is causally necessary for conscious perception
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The field's strict operational criterion is stated to OVERESTIMATE the thing it measures: subjects perform above chance while denying they perceived anything.
span.note: what this limits: a chance-level performance criterion as the test of non-conscious processing: the review states it tends to overestimate conscious perception, because subjects can perform above chance and still deny perceiving the stimulus
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Which task counts as evidence is unresolved, because performance can be at chance on one task and not another.
span.note: what this limits: a null result on one task as evidence of non-conscious processing: the review states performance can be at chance for some tasks but not others, leaving which tasks count unresolved
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The verdict rests on accepting a null hypothesis, and the review states the significance often depends on an analyst's choice of how many trials to run.
span.note: what this limits: any published claim that a stimulus was processed non-consciously: the review states performance never really falls to zero and that significance often depends on arbitrary choices such as the number of trials used to measure it

span.label: conscious access - BY THE OBJECTIVE CRITERION: a stimulus counts as non-conscious only if subjects cannot perform above chance on a direct task, a tradition grounded in signal-detection theory
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: conscious access - BY SUBJECTIVE CRITERIA: visibility ratings, or second-order commentaries such as post-decision wagering, adopted BECAUSE the objective criterion fails
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: attention - James's classic definition, which the review says CONFLATES two processes that are now clearly separable
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `conscious` - ONE WORD SPLIT BY GRAMMAR, NOT BY FIELD OR BY DATE. `“CONSCIOUS” IS AN AMBIGUOUS WORD. IN ITS INTRANSITIVE USE (e.g. "the patient was still conscious"), IT REFERS TO THE STATE OF CONSCIOUSNESS ... IN ITS TRANSITIVE USE (e.g. "I was not conscious of the red light"), IT REFERS TO CONSCIOUS ACCESS.` **The disambiguating test is whether the word takes an object.** Every other split in this corpus runs across disciplines, across decades, or across languages; this one runs across a syntactic frame, and the paper hands the reader a grammatical test rather than a definition.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `selection` / `selective attention` - AN ALIAS INTRODUCED IN PASSING AND THEN USED TO BREAK A FOLK IDENTITY. `SELECTION, ALSO CALLED SELECTIVE ATTENTION, REFERS TO the separation of relevant versus irrelevant information`, and the paper immediately reports that `SELECTION CAN OCCUR WITHOUT CONSCIOUS PROCESSING`. The naming matters because the everyday word `attention` carries the implication that attending is being aware, and the paper is dismantling exactly that.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across many paradigms, conscious access is marked by three convergent physiological signatures: late amplification of the relevant sensory activity, long-distance cortico-cortical synchronisation in the beta and gamma bands, and ignition of a large-scale prefronto-parietal network.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Subliminal influence shrinks as processing depth increases, leaving only small effects at high-level cognitive and decision stages.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Subliminal priming decays with time and is typically undetectable beyond about 500 ms.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Subliminal stimuli do not produce durable or flexible changes in executive control.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The first roughly 200 ms of visual processing is fully preserved on trials where the subject reports not seeing the stimulus, so early sensory activity does not distinguish conscious from non-conscious trials.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The most reliable electrophysiological correlate of visibility is the late, broadly distributed positive P3/P3b component at about 300-500 ms, distinct from the earlier focal anterior P3a which can occur non-consciously.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In monkeys viewing binocular rivalry, the share of neurons whose firing follows the reported percept rises steeply from primary visual cortex to higher associative cortex, supporting the idea that conscious assemblies are denser in higher areas.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Conscious words modulated late activity at 68.8% of intracranial electrode sites versus 24.4% for non-conscious words, showing that conscious access has a brain-wide impact.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Transcranial magnetic stimulation over parietal or prefrontal cortex, far from visual areas, can block conscious perception and even make a fixated stimulus subjectively disappear.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Patients with focal prefrontal lesions needed stronger stimuli to see a masked target, in proportion to how far the lesion extended into left anterior prefrontal cortex, while their subliminal performance stayed normal.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Early-stage multiple sclerosis patients, whose white-matter damage disrupts long-distance connectivity, required a longer target-mask delay before a stimulus became conscious.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The GNW model predicts and its simulations reproduce a strict seriality of conscious access, so only one content can be consciously processed at a time.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Subliminal no-go signals activate only a small set of specialised inhibitory processors, whereas conscious no-go signals additionally recruit anterior cingulate, inferior and middle frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal and inferior parietal cortex.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Schizophrenic patients show impaired neural signatures of conscious access while their subliminal processing remains normal.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The review's inventory of empirical markers of conscious access is: all-or-none prefronto-parietal ignition, all-or-none amplification of sensory activation, a late global P3b, late broad-band gamma power increase, enhanced long-distance beta-band phase synchronisation, and enhanced causal coupling between distant areas including a top-down component.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
